ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against Luxembourg national sanctions lists, CSSF AML/CFT regime, UN Security Council sanctions, EU Sanctions List (CFSP), OFAC SDN list, and PEP databases for all general partners, limited partners, managers, and beneficial owners. Enhanced due diligence required where any PEP identification occurs. Screening must be completed prior to registration and updated on an event-driven basis.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) interface for the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) – www.lbr.lu / available through Guichet.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SCSp name must be stated in French, German, Luxembourgish, or any other language using Latin script. In case non-Latin script is used, a French or German transcription is mandatory. The name must contain the suffix 'SCSp' or 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or its German equivalent 'Spezielle Kommanditgesellschaft'. Name shall not conflict with existing legal entities, trademarks, or create confusion with public bodies.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection by the RCS, the applicant may submit an administrative appeal to the Minister of Justice (Ministère de la Justice) within 40 days from the receipt of the rejection decision. The appeal must state the reasons for contestation and include the proposed name, the RCS decision reference, and legal arguments demonstrating non-conflict. If the Ministry upholds the rejection, the applicant may bring an action before the Luxembourg administrative tribunal within 3 months. An alternative name may be re-filed at any time.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office acceptance is conditional and generally permissible for the SCSp only if the virtual office provider offers a physical service address in Luxembourg, mail handling, and access to meeting space; however, the RCS and tax administration may reject a purely mail-drop address. For trade-remedy defense consulting activity, a physical presence in Luxembourg is strongly advisable and will satisfy statutory substance expectations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low_Risk_Virtual_Office_Moderate: estimated 15% annual probability of unannounced on-site inspection by RCS or tax authorities where only a virtual office is used; estimated 5% where a full-service physical office is maintained.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Articles 101-1 et seq. (société en commandite spéciale); Law of 23 July 2016 introducing the SCSp; Law of 19 December 2020 on the Register of Beneficial Owners.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Ministry of Justice, Luxembourg.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for RCS registration and the partnership agreement (convention de société), with mandatory RESA publication.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital; SCSp has no legal capital or escrow-account requirement. Contributions are due as set forth in the partnership agreement and may be denominated in any freely convertible currency.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: We, the general partner and the initial special partners of the undersigned société en commandite spéciale, acting by written resolution, hereby approve and record the following formation actions. First, the subscription of partnership interests and the contribution schedule set out in the partnership agreement are accepted in full. Second, the registered office of the partnership is fixed at [address], Luxembourg, and the RCS is designated as the competent registry for the statutory filing. Third, the general partner is appointed managing partner, and the following officers are appointed with joint signature authority: [names]. Fourth, the authorised representatives are directed to execute all registration documents, publish the RESA extract and undertake the establishment-authorisation application for ISIC 7490 trade-remedy defense consulting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve corporate name and execute the SCSp partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet.lu and Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR – RCS name search)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Check the availability of the proposed SCSp name in the RCS database, secure a registered office or domiciliation address in Luxembourg, collect KYC/beneficial-ownership data, and execute the partnership agreement by all partners. If the agreement is not notarised, each partner's signature must be certified.
required_dossiers: Identity and proof of address of each partner
AML/KYC file for general and special partners
Registered office lease or domiciliation agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, select a new distinctive name and re-verify; cure any missing KYC/beneficial-ownership information before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File for RCS registration and RESA publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the RCS registration application electronically via the LBR e-filing portal or with the assistance of a notary/accountant. Pay the statutory filing fee. When approved, the RCS issues the registration number and publishes the mandatory legal extract in RESA.
required_dossiers: RCS application form signed by the general partner
Identity documents of general partner and managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If queried, file the requested corrections through LBR within the administrative deadline; supply certified translations or additional due-diligence documents; re-pay any publication supplement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete tax, VAT and social security registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the RCS registration number to obtain the Luxembourg business identification number. Register with the AEDT for a Luxembourg VAT number if B2B consulting services are supplied; register with the CCSS if any employees are engaged. Provide the partnership agreement and beneficial-ownership details to the tax authorities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File an amended VAT application and provide further evidence of place of supply; update ACD/CCSS files retroactively; respond to information notices before assessments are raised.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Department of Establishment Permits / Guichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the 'autorisation d'établissement' through the Guichet.lu e-space. Attach the RCS extract, good-conduct certificates, professional qualifications of the managers and proof of premises. The authorised scope covers anti-dumping and trade-remedy defense consulting as a non-regulated commercial service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If refusal or objection is raised, adapt the requested professional scope, provide additional qualification evidence, or appeal to the Minister of the Economy within the statutory period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Secure environmental, civil defence and occupational safety clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development; Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS); Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Assess whether the office premises require a classified-installation declaration under environmental rules; for an office-based consulting activity it is normally exempt. Obtain the CGDIS fire-safety attestation for the premises and an ITM-compliant workplace risk assessment before employees begin work.
required_dossiers: Building occupation permit or lease file
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Remedy fire-safety and structural-load deficiencies and obtain re-inspection; file a supplementary environmental compliance file if waste/air emission thresholds are exceeded; implement and document an ITM corrective action plan.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Department of Establishment Permits / Guichet.lu
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement for ISIC 7490 trade-remedy defense consulting (business/establishment permit)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development (MECDD)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no full EIA Report is required for an office-based consulting activity under the Luxembourg EIA regime; a classified-installation declaration may be necessary only if the office floor area or any combustion equipment crosses the Class 4 thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC discharge is generated by the trade-defense consulting activity. Any backup generator or heating equipment must comply with the Luxembourg combustion air-emission limit values (NOx, CO, particulate matter); office waste must be separated and removed by an authorised collector.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: CGDIS fire-safety attestation for the premises; structural load inspection of any heavy equipment or archive floors; ITM workplace clearance including risk assessment, first-aid provisions, fire exits and employee health-and-safety training.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) is the competent authority for VAT registration and indirect taxes; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) is competent for direct income taxes; centralized e-government portal and e-filing platform: MyGuichet.lu (https://guichet.public.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Engage a Luxembourg-resident authorised representative or registered office provider. 2. Execute the SCSp partnership agreement and file the registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via the MyGuichet.lu e-Registration service, obtaining the RCS matricule (national business registration number used as the base tax identification number). 3. Submit the VAT registration application ('Inscription à la TVA', e-form 563) to the AEDT, attaching the RCS extract, partnership agreement, authorization of the legal representative and, for non-EU persons, designation of a Luxembourg VAT representative. 4. The AEDT issues the Luxembourg VAT identification number (LU + 8 digits) and, where customs activity is contemplated, the EORI number. No minimum capital is required for an SCSp.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists. Under Article 175 LIR as amended in 2016, an SCSp is fiscally transparent by default, but it is treated as opaque (subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax) where all of its partners are corporate entities subject to Luxembourg CIT or comparable corporate taxes. The tax classification is therefore determined by the statutory partner-composition criteria rather than by a formal filing election; partnership deed drafting and partner identity may be structured accordingly. Cross-border effects are further governed by the hybrid mismatch rules implemented by the Law of 21 December 2020 (ATAD 2), which may recharacterise transparent or opaque treatment in anti-hybrid situations.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT/TVA) governed by the amended Law of 12 February 1979 on VAT (Loi TVA) and Directive 2006/112/EC (EU VAT Directive)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 30,000 annual turnover threshold for the domestic small-business franchise exemption (Article 57 Loi TVA) applicable only to Luxembourg-established businesses; non-resident suppliers have no registration exemption and must register before making the first taxable supply in Luxembourg. A separate EUR 10,000 annual threshold applies to intra-EU distance sales and B2C electronic/telecom/broadcasting services under the Union One-Stop-Shop (OSS) regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently operate real-time fiscal clearance, government API stamping, or continuous transaction controls (CTC). B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary and is based on Peppol/Factur-X interoperability standards. E-invoicing is mandatory only in the B2G segment for invoices addressed to central public-sector contracting authorities. Under the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) package, mandatory intra-EU B2B e-invoicing and digital reporting are expected to apply from 1 July 2030, subject to Luxembourg transposition.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: export supplies to third countries and persons outside the EU qualify for the 0% rate where the goods physically leave the EU within 90 days of supply and the exporter retains acceptable proof of export (Article 38 Loi TVA, transposing Article 146 VAT Directive). Services: anti-dumping defense and trade-remedy consulting services supplied to a non-resident business customer are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT under B2B place-of-supply rules (customer's establishment, with reverse charge); services to a non-taxable person established outside the EU are excluded from Luxembourg VAT where effectively used and enjoyed outside the EU. Intra-EU B2B consulting services are reverse-charged to the EU customer and reported in the Luxembourg EC Sales List without Luxembourg VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (SAD/electronic declaration) released by Luxembourg Customs (ADER)
Bill of Lading, CMR consignment note or air waybill evidencing physical exit of goods from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent SWIFT/bank transfer confirmation evidencing receipt of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEDT and Luxembourg Customs (ADER) apply targeted substantive audit scrutiny to export zero-rating and refund claims. Failure to substantiate the export within the statutory conditions causes reversal of the 0% rate and assessment of Luxembourg VAT at 17%, together with late-payment interest of 0.6% per month and a 10% payment surcharge. Willful or fraudulent claims additionally expose the taxpayer to criminal tax-fraud sanctions (imprisonment of up to 5 years and/or fines of up to EUR 250,000). The ordinary reassessment limitation period is five years, extended to ten years in cases of fraud, and refunds already paid out are subject to retrospective clawback with interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) acting within the Eurosystem framework of the European Central Bank (ECB), with the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance and the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) supervising banking and foreign exchange intermediation conduct.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a Eurozone member state with fully liberalised capital and current account transactions under EU Treaty provisions on free movement of capital and the EU Capital Requirements Regulation. No exchange control legislation restricts the conversion of EUR into foreign currency or vice versa. Capital account transactions, including the injection of foreign equity into a Luxembourg SCSp, profit distribution to non-resident limited partners, and repayment of shareholder loans, are unrestricted. Profit remittance is subject only to general anti-money-laundering, tax compliance (including potential withholding formalities under EU Directives or treaty-based reductions), and verification of economic substance where tax treaty benefits are claimed. For cross-border trade in services such as anti-dumping defence legal consulting, current account receivables and payments are freely convertible without prior authorisation or surrender requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory duty to surrender export proceeds to the central bank or any governmental authority, and no mandatory conversion ratio applies to export receipts. All proceeds from exports of services, including legal and consultancy fees in anti-dumping trade defence matters, may be retained in EUR or any other freely convertible currency in bank accounts held domestically or abroad, subject to standard reporting obligations under the EU Balance of Payments statistics and the Luxembourg General Tax Code for accounting and tax record-keeping.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational EUR/USD Account and segregated Capital Escrow Account for LP capital contributions
Operational Account and dedicated Capital Escrow Account under the SCSp agreement
Operational Account with a parallel Capital Escrow Account for non-resident investor funds

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational EUR Account and Capital Escrow Account for regulatory and escrow-controlled disbursements
Operational Account only; seamless SEPA and SWIFT clearing for cross-border advisory fee invoicing

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. The viability of offshore digital e-money institutions and electronic money institutions (EMIs) for the SCSp treasury is constrained by the requirement for EU/EEA authorisation and passporting rights. A third-country EMI, particularly a UK-based entity post-Brexit, generally has no passporting right to provide payment services to a Luxembourg-domiciled client without a Luxembourg licence or equivalent licensing; such offshore providers are therefore not recommended for primary clearing rails. EEA-licensed EMIs may operate under the Second Payment Services Directive (PSD2) but typically impose account limits, restrict high-value trade settlements, and require additional KYC for pass-through vehicles. For a professional anti-dumping defence consultancy, a fully licensed Luxembourg bank remains the preferred legal and treasury counterparty, while a regulated EMI can be used for low-value, subsidiary expense disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg AML/KYC rules under the Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF circulars require regulated banks to identify and verify the beneficial owner, general partner, and authorised signatories of an SCSp. Remote onboarding using video identification is legally possible and accepted by most banks under CSSF remote-identification guidelines, provided the process is conducted through a certified provider and the final KYC file is reviewed by the compliance team. In practice, for a non-resident general partner or for an SCSp with complex foreign limited partners, the bank's compliance officer will require at least one physical or video-conference interview with the general partner or its authorized representative before account opening; static documents alone rarely suffice. A fully physical appearance mandate arises only in higher-risk scenarios, e.g., unexplained source of funds or dealings with sanctioned jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained source of wealth of non-resident limited partners or beneficial owners contributing capital into the SCSp.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Latest bank statements of the contributor evidencing origin of funds; audited or certified financial statements; personal tax returns for the relevant periods; notarised declaration of source of wealth and source of funds; commercial reference letters from an existing regulated financial institution; corporate formation documents and register extracts of the contributor; and a clear written explanation of the economic purpose of the capital contribution aligned with the SCSp's trade defence consulting business plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through partnership structure without demonstrable economic substance or with opaque intra-group transactions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Duly executed and notarised limited partnership agreement (LPA); Luxembourg RCS registration extract and registered office address certificate; domiciliation agreement; management accounts and cash flow projections; detailed board or general partner minutes approving the anti-dumping trade defence engagement; evidence of physical office or administrative presence in Luxembourg, including lease agreements, employee payslips and timesheets; and a documented explanation of how consulting fees are earned through the SCSp's own activities rather than via conduit or round-tripping arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions involving high-risk jurisdictions or sanctioned counterparties in the anti-dumping value chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated sanctions and PEP screening results with no match or a mitigated explanation; engagement letter of the legal consultancy showing the precise defence trade-remedy scope; underlying export/import trade documentation and customs case files; production of inquiry notices from the European Commission or national investigating authority; a sworn statement by the ultimate beneficial owner on the absence of directly or indirectly sanctioned parties; and enhanced due diligence reports on the client and its supply chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid inbound capital injection followed by intended outbound transfers to external law firms or expert witnesses without clear commercial linkage.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution approving the specific capital call and expenditure budget; signed agreements with external counsels and expert economic consultants; itemized fee schedules tied to the anti-dumping questionnaire response, injury analysis, or other legal deliverables; expected disbursement timetable; SWIFT wire instructions with precise purpose references; and a reconciliation statement showing that the commercial chain is transparent and corresponds to actual legal services performed.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions from non-resident limited partners or foreign investors into the Luxembourg SCSp are executed through standard SWIFT MT103 or equivalent SEPA/SEPA Instant credit transfers. There is no exchange-control approval requirement. The bank transfer should identify the beneficiary as the exact SCSp legal name and account number, with the remittance information line stating 'Capital Contribution – SCSp Subscription Agreement reference [document number]'. Additional documentary verification comprises the executed subscription/capital call agreement, the board resolution of the general partner, a passport copy and proof of address of the contributor, and a source-of-funds statement where the contributed amount exceeds the bank's threshold. For statistical purposes, the receiving bank may request a Luxembourg Balance of Payments (BoP) declaration; the applicable purpose code is generally 'Direct Investment – Equity Capital' (BoP code E1/C2 or equivalent local coding) for equity injections, or 'Loan to affiliated enterprise' for shareholder loans. Upon clearance, the funds are credited to the operational or dedicated capital escrow ledger from which trade defence expenses and legal fees are subsequently paid.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and professional fee disbursements from the SCSp are settled over either SWIFT MT103 for cross-border non-EUR transactions or SEPA and TARGET2 for EUR payments within the EEA. Commercial letters of credit (documentary L/C under UCP600) are available for underlying trade flows connected with the anti-dumping investigation, including import-export transactions where the consulting firm supports importer or exporter evidence collection. For direct payments to foreign counsel, expert economists, survey firms, and government filing agencies, the bank requires a written payment instruction from the general partner, proof of invoiced services, and a description referencing the ISO 20022 purpose code such as 'LEGL' (legal services) or 'PRMF' (professional fees). The same clearing rails also support SWIFT MT202 cover for interbank settlement when multiple currency legs are involved. High-value EUR payments are finally cleared through TARGET2 to guarantee immediate, irrevocable settlement; SWIFT MT103 remains the industry standard for outbound USD clearing and for non-European jurisdictions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX spot contracts for same-day or T+2 settlement
Outright vanilla FX forward contracts with non-bank or bank counterparties, unencumbered by exchange controls
Foreign exchange options (vanilla call and put options) entered into to hedge advisory fee receivables or payables in non-EUR currencies
Cross-currency swaps (fixed-for-floating or floating-for-fixed) for longer-term balance-sheet hedging of foreign-denominated capital losses or asset exposures

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or non-convertible currencies, subject to EMIR trade reporting, margining obligations if the counterparty is above clearing thresholds, and internal risk-policy approvals

Listed currency futures traded on regulated EU markets, provided the SCSp's treasury mandate expressly authorises exchange-traded derivatives and post-trade clearing through a qualifying central counterparty

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (comptes annuels) or exemption declaration for SCSp whose general partner is a legal entity subject to equivalent publication obligations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) via LBR (Luxembourg Business Registers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the end of the financial year; for a 31 December year-end, filing due by 31 July; exemption available where the general partner (gérant) is a corporate entity filing its own accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court order compelling filing; daily penalty up to EUR 5,000 for continued non-compliance; criminal fines against managing partners; repeated failure leads to administrative strike-off (radiation d'office) from the RCS and loss of legal existence

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership declaration (UBO register annual recertification)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) via LBR (Luxembourg Business Registers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Once per calendar year, due before 31 December of each year irrespective of whether ownership changed; any ownership change during the year triggers an update filing within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines ranging from EUR 125 to EUR 125,000 per order; criminal fines up to EUR 25,000 and imprisonment of 6 months to 5 years for beneficial owners and managing partners; publication of a corrective judgment at the entity's cost; persistent non-filing supports forced RBE registration and is a trigger for administrative strike-off proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) annual return for the SCSp's commercial trade-defense consulting activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: ACD (Administration des contributions directes) on behalf of the commune of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual return due by 31 May of the following year; automatic extension to 31 December when filed electronically; quarterly advance instalments payable on 15 February, 15 May, 15 August and 15 November of the current year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties up to EUR 25,000 at the tax collector's discretion; default surcharge (majoration d'impôt) of 10% of assessed tax; monthly late-payment interest at the statutory rate; distraint, attachment of bank accounts and forced recovery against the partnership's assets and the general partner

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax and net wealth tax annual returns (only applicable if the SCSp has elected opaque taxation or holds a Luxembourg business establishment operated through a fixed commercial structure)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 31 May of the following year; electronic filing extends the deadline to 31 December; final assessment may be issued within 5 years from the end of the year in which the tax becomes chargeable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default surcharge of 10% on any assessed balance; monthly interest of 0.6% on overdue amounts; criminal fines where a false return is filed knowingly; repeated default may justify forced liquidation by the Public Prosecutor

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT annual return (annual summary declaration) and periodic monthly or quarterly VAT returns for professional services subject to Luxembourg VAT at the standard rate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: AEDT (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual summary declaration due by 30 April of the following year; monthly VAT returns due by the 15th day of the following month; quarterly returns due by the 15th day of the following quarter for taxpayers below the threshold; e-Filing is mandatory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil fine of EUR 250 to EUR 10,000 per unfiled or late periodic return; 10% surcharge on late VAT payable; monthly default interest; criminal prosecution for intentional omission with fines up to double the evaded tax and imprisonment of the managing partner

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit (by an approved réviseur d'entreprises) applies where the SCSp exceeds two of the three following criteria at the balance-sheet date: balance sheet total exceeds EUR 4,400,000; net turnover exceeds EUR 8,800,000; average number of full-time employees during the financial year exceeds 50; small and micro SCSp are exempt unless the SCSp is a public fund, a UCITS, an alternative investment fund with manager obligations, or is required by its constitutional document to appoint an auditor
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP per the Law of 19 December 2002 on the commercial register and annual accounts (transposing EU Directive 2013/34/EU), with the option to apply IFRS for large undertakings and for entities whose securities are admitted to trading; SCSp tax transparency is recognised for fiscal purposes through the qualification of the partnership as a fiscally transparent vehicle under article 175bis of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must maintain an internal register of beneficial owners and file the UBO declaration with the RBE structural pillar; the annual confirmation must be completed once each calendar year before 31 December even where no shareholder movement occurred; because the SCSp is fully transparent, each limited partner holding an economic interest is disassembled to the ultimate natural person except where a partner is a governmental entity or a listed company, and the managing general partner must certify accuracy; any share transfer or contribution change mandates an updated declaration submitted to the RBE within 30 days; the UBO register is not open to the general public but is accessible to the financial intelligence unit, the tax administration, notaries and gauged relevant professional parties with a justified interest
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (register of limited partners and general partner with ownership percentages and dates of admission)
Register of Managers (gérants) with signatures and powers of representation
Minute Book (register of partner resolutions and management decisions)
Register of Beneficial Owners (internal UBO register reconciled with the RBE filing)
Register of Accounting Documents (annual accounts, audit reports and tax reconciliation statements)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 - 4,000 per annum for licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent, registered office and corporate secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - 22,000 per annum for a certified statutory audit by a Luxembourg réviseur d'entreprises when the large-undertaking thresholds are exceeded; preparation-only review for small SCSp typically ranges USD 2,500 - 6,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate for Luxembourg City (17.00% corporate income tax + 1.19% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax) applicable to corporate partners on taxable profits above EUR 175,000; reduced 22.80% rate on the first EUR 175,000 bracket
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is tax-transparent, so incentives apply at partner level. Principal Luxembourg CIT incentives: 80% exemption on qualifying IP box income resulting in an effective 4.99% CIT on net IP profits; notional interest deduction (NID) computed on qualifying new equity; 20% super-deduction for qualifying research and development expenditure; Start-up/innovation carve-outs do not otherwise alter the statutory CIT for trade-remedy consulting income.
